brief:
Gaza's journalists endure severe mental health pressures while covering the territory's ongoing conflict, according to We Are Not Numbers. Reporters work amid conditions of constant fear, loss, displacement, hunger, and danger—circumstances that shape both their professional assignments and their personal survival. The psychological strain intensifies because journalists document crises that simultaneously threaten their own families and livelihoods.

The burden distinguishes Gaza reporting from conventional war coverage. Correspondents cannot separate themselves from the events they chronicle; they experience displacement from their homes, food shortages, and security threats while maintaining professional duties to gather and transmit information to outside audiences. This collapse of distance between observer and subject creates compounded trauma that extends far beyond standard occupational stress.
dek: We are living what we are reporting: fear, loss, displacement, hunger, danger.
title: Gaza journalists grapple with psychological toll while covering their own crisis
